title: Make graph recovery handle persisted hostile work text without rejecting the whole export
outcome: Make graph recovery carry the persisted text, historical actors and gate history a live store holds, byte-exact, without rejecting the whole export
acceptance: A fixture reproducing the persisted ESC-bearing cancelled work items can be exported and restored through the chosen documented graph recovery contract without dropping work items, relations, or history, and without rendering terminal controls unsafely.

New work-text admission and graph snapshot validation agree: a regression test covers ordinary add/update and save/load, proving admitted titles can be exported or the title is explicitly refused before its write.

The implementation explicitly resolves historical stored text outside any new admission rule, preserves original durable records and ids, and reports any deliberately transformed recovery fields rather than silently changing them.

A graph save and load rehearsal against an authorized coherent copy of the affected Engram store succeeds, or names every remaining offending field with actionable work/record context; no live data is edited merely to make the exporter pass.

completion.summary: graph save/load carry stored text byte-exact: persisted prose is non-empty and trimmed only, with controls carried and escaped on render; memory bodies keep their whitespace; gate history uses the stored gate rules; work-history actors use the write-path shape; memory version and tombstone actors use the project-memory attribution rule; the operator keeps the strict audit shape; the saved container escapes every terminal-unsafe character. Rehearsed on a read-only copy of the live Engram store (939 items, byte-exact). Two review rounds; round 2 is clean (one docs Note). Gate test-9201abf1 passed; the independent evaluation passed 4/4.
